tagline: Every person matters. Every search counts.
demo: Frontend demo · No real reports are filed
heroTop: A little hope. A collective effort.
heroDesc: A familiar face. A place. A small detail. Start with what you know. KHOJ helps bring the pieces together, in your own language.
freeLine: Searching police records from Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Chandigarh. More states soon.
introDesc: When someone goes missing, every detail matters. Describe what you know, in the language you know. We’ll help you take the next step.
howDesc: Describe the person in one complete reply, by voice or text. KHOJ organizes the details, marks what is still unknown, and lets you review everything before saving.
exampleText: My brother Rahul is about 24. He speaks Hindi, was wearing a blue shirt, and has a scar on his left eyebrow. He was last seen near New Delhi station on Friday evening.
exampleReply: Here’s what I understood from your description. The known details are listed below; anything you didn’t mention stays unknown.
reviewNote: You review every detail before saving.
togetherLabel: A LITTLE INFORMATION CAN GO A LONG WAY
togetherDesc: Families, people who want to help, and reviewing officers each have a part to play. KHOJ is designed to connect the details while protecting the person.
familyRoleDesc: A description, a recent photo, a place to start.
officerRoleDesc: Possible leads checked by a person.
storyDesc: Technology can help connect details. It takes people to bring someone home.
principle1desc: Speak or type in English or Hindi. You don’t need to know the right form or the right words.
principle2:
Small details.
A place to start.
principle2desc: Share everything you know in one reply. Details you don’t mention remain unknown, ready to review together.
principle3:
A possible lead.
A human review.
principle3desc: A similarity is never a confirmed identity. A reviewing officer must check every possible match.
feature1desc: Report someone missing, share a found-person report, or search by description.
feature2desc: Speak or type one complete description. We help organize it into clear, reviewable details.
feature3desc: Review the details extracted from your description. Check what is known, edit anything, and confirm before saving.
feature4desc: A found person’s photo and location are never shown to searchers.
feature5desc: Designed for daily checks when the backend is connected.
feature6desc: Possible matches need officer review before anyone is contacted.
faq1a: KHOJ is a frontend concept that helps people in India describe a missing or found person, review a report, and search for possible similarities. This version uses demo data.
faq2: Does KHOJ replace a police report?
faq2a: No. Contact the police to file an official missing-person report. KHOJ is designed to support a search; it does not replace official reporting or emergency services.
faq3: Can I use my own language?
faq3a: English and Hindi are available. Marathi, Bengali, Tamil, and Punjabi are planned; their translation files are included for future translation.
faq4: Who can see a found person’s details?
faq4a: Found-person photos and locations are not shown in public search results. A connected service must route potential leads to authorized reviewers.
faq5: Is this connected to police records?
faq5a: This is a working frontend demo. Search results are fictional, OTP uses a demo code, and reports are saved only on this device. No police notification is sent.
ctaDesc: You don’t need every answer. Start with what you know.
footerSafety: A possible match always needs a human review.

helpIntro: In an emergency, contact local emergency services. KHOJ is not an emergency service.
helpReportingDesc: Contact your local police station for official reporting. Keep a recent photo and any useful details ready. Do not wait for a KHOJ result to seek help.
